title: Ice

exclude: Playfield matrix buffers. The viewport draw at $185D, $1897 and $18BD generates 800 character cells in the first buffer, and the loop at $1916 mirrors its four pages to the second. The remaining cells lie past the displayed playfield rows. The sprite writer uses the final eight addresses of both matrices as pointer registers.

Resident release code from the language load. Bytes are identical at the language and quest hand-overs and the quest load write map records no stores in this interval. The entry reads the resident byte at $C980.
Processor port and zero-page workspace. $3B3D clears bytes $02–$FF and the game fills individual pointers, control masks and counters as it runs.
Installed software interrupt and KERNAL vectors. The quest IRQ setup patches $0316 and $0317 during initialization.
Object-construction scratch filled by the map action and deferred spawn paths before they call $1940.
Intermediate object piece positions, sprite bytes and count generated by $1DA6 and filtered by $1E61.
The per-frame sprite list arrays. $2127 fills them from object, item and projectile state before raster display.
New viewport character edge buffers produced by the renderers and copied into the next matrix by the scroll routines.
Generated viewport edge colours. The edge builders translate the character bytes through the world colour table before these values are copied to colour RAM.
Generated hardware sprite pointers for the spell HUD. The setup and selection routines write these pointer bytes from the active spell indices.
Generated 256-byte unpacked map action row. $37AD fills it from the stored compressed row. The spell display also fills its first 64 bytes with $AA.
Six object slots represented as separate per-field arrays. The constructor at $1940 fills the active slot, and the following object-motion code updates those fields.
include: Authored sprite shapes, fetched by the VIC in bank $C000.

regions: Quest sprite slots, 63 bitmap bytes plus one byte per slot
